walkthroughs.body_html:
Introduction to Religions (Two from: Buddhism, Christianity, Hinduism, Islam, Judaism, Sikhism, Baha'i, Jainism, Taoism, Indigenous Religions) — a core area of Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Introduction to Religions (Two from: Buddhism, Christianity, Hinduism, Islam, Judaism, Sikhism, Baha'i, Jainism, Taoism, Indigenous Religions) brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Introduction to Religions (Two from: Buddhism, Christianity, Hinduism, Islam, Judaism, Sikhism, Baha'i, Jainism, Taoism, Indigenous Religions).

The Shahada is the Islamic pilgrimage to Mecca.
The Shahada is the requirement to pray five times a day.
The Eightfold Path is eight gods Buddhists must please.
The Islamic declaration of faith: 'There is no god but Allah, and Muhammad is the messenger of Allah' — affirming monotheism and Muhammad's prophethood.

mcqs.q: What is the Eightfold Path in Buddhism?
options: The Eightfold Path is eight gods Buddhists must please.
Substance dualism means men and women are different.

The practical path to ending suffering: right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration — grouped into wisdom, ethical conduct and mental discipline.
The Eightfold Path is the same as the Four Noble Truths.

mcqs.q: What is substance dualism about mind and body?
options: Substance dualism is the belief that humans have two personalities.
Substance dualism means men and women are different.
The view (associated with Descartes) that mind and body are two distinct kinds of substance — a non-physical mind interacting with a physical body.
The Eightfold Path is eight gods Buddhists must please.
